title: Display Name Fallback
prompt: A TypeScript profile card can receive first and last names, but some accounts only have a username. Write a function that returns "first last" when both names exist, otherwise returns the username.

explanation.beginner:
Example: displayNameFallback({"firstName":"Ada","lastName":"Lovelace","username":"ada"}) produces "Ada Lovelace". Identify exactly which values mean absent under the contract, then select the fallback only for those values.

Compare “falls back to username”: input [{"firstName":"Ada","username":"ada"}] produces "ada". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Identify exactly which values mean absent under the contract, then select the fallback only for those values.

Tempting mistake: A truthiness check also replaces 0, false, and an empty string. Nullish absence and falsiness are different rules.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “falls back to username”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
